tenet: Use state machines / typestate — an invalid transition must not compile
why_discriminating: The easy/naive solution is a runtime-checked builder (Option fields, build() throws if url unset). The skillful solution moves the state into a phantom type parameter so `build()` is only available once a URL has been set (e.g. an extension on RequestBuilder[HasUrl]), making `RequestBuilder().build()` a compile error. The prompt is NEUTRAL — it states the domain (url required, method optional) but not the type-level solution.
prompt: Implement an HTTP request builder in Scala 3. A request has a required URL and an optional HTTP method. Expose a public `RequestBuilder` constructed with `RequestBuilder()`, with a `.url(url: String)` method, an optional `.method(method: String)` method, and a `.build()` method returning the finished request. Output top-level definitions only — no `@main`, no tests.
